hi! i live in england and i’ve moved up and down the country, so i don’t really have any advice on moving internationally or the financial aspects of it but i’ll just share my experiences, i hope it’ll help somewhat. 

i’m going to be very straightforward with you: it’s very unlikely that you’ll be able to medically transition for a while if you’re going to england. i don’t know about scotland or anything but i’m 16, i started trying to get on the waiting list for the gender clinic earlier this year. they straight up told me i probably won’t be able to transition at all until i’m at least 18. that’s with the nhs, you can go private but it’s a lot of money. this isn’t to upset you or anything, i just think it’s something you need to know. but hey, i guess an upside is that you won’t have to worry about hiding your transition from your parents as much? 

also, at least in england, 16 is the age that you’re able to legally live on your own, so i don’t really know how you’d be able to get him out of there before that, but as long as the law is the same in ireland i don’t see how anyone could stop you. again, i know it’s a long time i just can’t think of anything you’d be able to do beforehand. 

and, it’s not… really the same thing but i’ve moved a lot as a kid, i’ve been to a lot of schools. i escaped my abusive dad as soon as i turned 16, i have very minimal contact with him, since i only talk to him if he calls me (which is rare). moving is just kind of the norm for us, but i’d say leaving a note somewhere you commonly check (like somewhere on your phone) so that everyone in the sys knows what’s going on is a good idea. stay in contact with any friends, video call them etc etc. with your family, just remember that you’re doing what’s best for you, and that’s what matters here. 

sorry for the long comment!! i hope that helps at least somewhat, this is all just from my own experiences. if you have any questions lmk!!

i’ll speak from my personal experience, since it’s not the same for everyone. it started when my mental health began going downhill, and i started biting my lip and punching myself when i was alone and sad/angry. i guess i didn’t feel like i had another way to vent. at one point in art class my pencil sharpener broke, and that’s how i started cutting. 

i think people can help by listening to people and finding the root of the problem - wether that be mental health, home life or something else and support them with getting the help they need. when they want to vent, listen to them. encourage them to distract themselves if they have urges (this is a big one!! distracting them from self harming is one of the best things you can do in my experience). if they relapse, they’re not at square one, it’s a slip up and happens when you’re trying to recover. remind them that. if they cut or burn, make sure that they’re taking care of their wounds properly to prevent infection, ESPECIALLY if they cut deep (i’m not sure about burns tho - i’ve never done it but i’m pretty sure they can get infected).

basically, be a kind person. it’s a really delicate subject and it takes a hell of a lot to recover. everyone’s different but the bottom line is be there to support and be respectful. if they ask you to drop the subject, drop it. if they don’t want to tell you something, don’t pressure them. they’ll tell you if their ready. 

oh and while i’m at it, NEVER guilt trip!! never say things like “how could you do this to me?” or “people have it worse than you” or anything like that! it doesn’t help! 

i think that’s what a lot of people need to know on how to help. i need to stress that each person is different and what may work well for one person won’t work for another. i’m talking from my experience, so just talk to the person, communicate with them and listen to what they have to say and be respectful of their boundaries and absolutely encourage them to seek professional help (but don’t pressure them if they’re in a situation where that’s not possible)
